name: Wheel hub and bearing
summary: The spinning mount that the brake disc and wheel bolt to. It runs on a bearing inside the steering knuckle.
whatItDoes: It lets the wheel spin freely while carrying the car's weight and the forces of cornering and braking.
howItWorks: A sealed bearing (rows of steel balls or rollers) sits between the fixed knuckle and the turning hub flange. Wheel studs pass through the flange: the brake disc slips over them, then the wheel. On driven wheels the CV axle passes through the middle of the hub. Many cars also put the ABS wheel-speed sensor here.
failureSymptoms: Humming or growling that gets louder with speed and changes when you turn
Play when you rock the wheel top to bottom
safetyNotes: Pressed-in bearings need a press. Hammering them in ruins them.
Tighten the axle nut to the figure in the manual: the bearing's preload depends on it.
